hypothesis: QQQ mean-reverts after closing below its 20-day lower Bollinger Band, but only in low-volatility regimes (current 20d realized vol <= trailing 1yr median); high-vol regimes are explicitly excluded because the prior SMA-crossover strategy (2026-09-01-001) failed walk-forward specifically due to regime-dependence around the 2022 rate-hike period.
rejection_reason: Sharpe ratio -0.30 vs required >= 1.0, a clear (non-borderline) fail on full-sample data (2019-2026, QQQ). Only 14 trades / 81 days in market over 7.7 years; strategy lost money on a risk-adjusted basis. Remaining validators (transaction costs, walk-forward, parameter sensitivity) skipped per RESEARCH_LOOP.md Step 5/6: a negative full-sample Sharpe cannot pass a stricter out-of-sample check, so running them would not change the outcome.
notes: Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY SMA crossover, trend-following, rejected on walk-forward) and 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate mean reversion, rejected on data feasibility) -- this is a QQQ mean-reversion idea with an explicit vol-regime filter designed to avoid exactly the regime-dependence that broke 2026-09-01-001. Vol-regime filter worked as intended (kept MDD to 15%, low market exposure), but the underlying entry signal itself has no discernible edge on QQQ daily bars. Two ideas for a future loop, recorded in the backtest report: (1) try a coarser Bollinger band (2.5-3 std) / shorter timeframe to get a stronger per-trade edge with fewer, higher-conviction trades; (2) the full-sample annualized Sharpe metric may unfairly penalize any low-market-exposure strategy during QQQ's 2019-2026 secular uptrend -- a days-in-market-only comparison could be a fairer validator refinement. Also fixed two real scaffold bugs this loop: vectorbt import was broken by plotly>=5.24 removing scattermapbox (pinned plotly<5.24 in requirements.txt), and validators.py check_sharpe_ratio/check_max_drawdown crashed with "Index frequency is None" (fixed by passing freq="D" explicitly to the vectorbt returns accessor).

notes: Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY dual-SMA crossover, equity, failed walk-forward) -- same trend-following family but different asset class and signal construction (single trailing-return threshold vs MA crossover); distinct from 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate mean reversion, rejected on data feasibility) -- this only needs OHLCV; distinct from 2026-09-03-001 (QQQ Bollinger mean-reversion, rejected on Sharpe) -- trend-following not mean-reversion, crypto not equity. hypothesis: BTC/USDT absolute momentum (45-day lookback) combined with an inverse-volatility position-size overlay (target 40% annualized vol, size capped at 1x) retains the Sharpe edge of shorter-lookback momentum while reducing max drawdown versus the pure binary-position 90-day momentum strategy (2026-09-03-002), by de-risking during high realized-vol regimes instead of full in/out exposure.
rejection_reason: Max drawdown 47.6% at the pre-registered 45d lookback (best-case 39.3% at 30d) still exceeds the 35% hard risk budget despite the vol-targeting overlay materially improving on the prior binary-position momentum strategy (66.0% MDD). Transaction-cost-survival also failed (net Sharpe 0.42 vs 0.5), though this is partly an artifact of the validator counting every daily vol-driven position-size change as a discrete trade (~1231 over 2801 days) rather than a realistic rebalance cadence.
notes: Direct follow-up to 2026-09-03-002 (BTC absolute momentum, 90d, rejected on MDD 66%): implements the vol-targeting/position-sizing overlay explicitly recommended in that entrys notes. Sharpe improved to 1.24 (passes) and MDD improved to 47.6% (still fails 35% budget) -- directional progress but insufficient. Parameter sensitivity passed (rel std 0.13). Distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY SMA crossover, equity) and 2026-09-03-001 (QQQ Bollinger mean-reversion, equity). Ideas for next loop: faster-reacting vol estimator (EWMA/short half-life) or a hard drawdown circuit-breaker stacked on top of continuous sizing, since 20-day realized vol lags sudden BTC crashes; also add a min_rebalance_threshold to check_transaction_cost_survival so continuous-sizing strategies arent penalized for daily vol noise. Walk-forward validator still broken (vbt.utils.splitting missing), unfixed since 2026-09-03-002.

hypothesis: A 200-day long-term SMA trend filter, ANDed with a medium-term (30-90d) absolute-momentum signal, reduces max drawdown on BTC/USDT and equity indices (SPY/QQQ) enough to clear the 35% hard risk budget, versus prior pure-momentum attempts (2026-09-03-002/-003) that failed MDD.
rejection_reason: Best grid config (mom_window=30, trend_window=200) fails full-sample validators on both tested asset classes: SPY misses Sharpe threshold narrowly (0.94 vs 1.0), BTC/USDT narrowly exceeds MDD budget (37.0% vs 35.0%). Both are near-misses (closest BTC has gotten to clearing MDD across three attempts), but neither clears the bar cleanly. Grid pass_fraction 40.3% overall, driven almost entirely by low-vol-regime cells (83% pass) vs mid/high-vol (33%/4%) -- the trend filter is regime-dependent, same failure mode that killed 2026-09-01-001.
notes: Source: https://github.com/IsaacDodds/crypto-momentum-backtest (README) -- found a 200d BTC trend filter roughly halves cross-sectional crypto momentum MDD (v1 -89.8% -> v2 -53.8%) at some Sharpe cost; this iteration tested the same trend-filter mechanism as an AND-gate on single-asset absolute momentum (distinct from the source, which used it on cross-sectional top-K selection). Also attempted https://www.quantifiedstrategies.com/trend-following-strategy-for-stocks/ (ATR trailing-stop rules) and https://pyquantlab.medium.com/dynamic-trailing-stops-using-atr-2d3c4e95ddc0 -- both blocked by bot-verification/Cloudflare, no content extracted (logged in visited_pages.jsonl as strategy_extracted=false so not re-fetched). Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SPY SMA crossover, rejected walk-forward), 2026-09-02-001 (BTC funding-rate, rejected feasibility), 2026-09-03-001 (QQQ Bollinger meanrev, rejected Sharpe), 2026-09-03-002 (BTC 90d absolute momentum, rejected MDD 66.0%), 2026-09-03-003 (BTC 45d momentum + vol-target, rejected MDD 47.6% + TC) -- this is the first attempt combining a long-horizon trend gate with momentum rather than vol-targeting, and gets closest yet to clearing BTC MDD (37.0%). Grid test used validation/grid_test.py::run_strategy_grid (mom_window x trend_window x 4 symbols x 3 vol terciles = 72 cells). Fixed a scaffold bug in validation/validators.py::check_transaction_cost_survival (was calling net_returns.vbt.returns.sharpe_ratio() without freq=D, raising ValueError on unset index frequency -- now net_returns.vbt.returns(freq="D").sharpe_ratio(), matching check_sharpe_ratio/check_max_drawdown pattern). Future idea: combine trend filter + vol-targeting overlay together (2026-09-03-003), or lengthen trend_window to 250-300d to reduce mid-vol-regime whipsaws.

hypothesis: Larry Connors RSI(2) mean-reversion (long-only): long when close > 200d SMA AND RSI(2) closes <= an oversold threshold (5 or 10), exit on close crossing back above the 5-day SMA; a fast (few-day) mean-reversion entry nested inside a long-term uptrend filter, exploiting short-term overreaction/oversold bounces distinct from the multi-week/month momentum family already tried in this repo.
rejection_reason: Crypto (BTC/USDT) at grid-best params (rsi_entry=10, trend_window=200) fails Sharpe (0.37 vs 1.0), MDD (36.4% vs 35%), and TC-adjusted Sharpe (0.26 vs 0.5) -- only parameter sensitivity passes. Not accepted for crypto at this parameterization.
notes: Source: https://chartschool.stockcharts.com/table-of-contents/trading-strategies-and-models/trading-strategies/rsi-2 (StockCharts writeup of Larry Connors RSI(2) strategy) -- rules taken directly: 200d SMA trend filter, RSI(2) oversold entry (5 or 10), 5d SMA cross exit. Long-only implementation (no shorting) per SAFETY.md/repo convention. Novelty: first RSI-oscillator/fast-mean-reversion-in-uptrend strategy tried here, distinct from 2026-09-01-001 (SMA crossover trend-following, rejected walk-forward), 2026-09-03-001 (Bollinger meanrev no trend filter, rejected Sharpe -0.30), 2026-09-03-002/-003/-004 (momentum family, all rejected on MDD). SPY full-sample: Sharpe 1.27, MDD 8.5%, TC-adj Sharpe 0.68, param-sensitivity rel.std 0.075 -- ACCEPT, all validators clean. Future idea: retest crypto with a crypto-tuned RSI(2)/trend-window parameterization rather than assuming the equity-optimized config transfers.

hypothesis: Turn-of-the-month (TOTM) calendar effect: long only during the last trading day of the month plus the first N trading days of the next month, flat otherwise, captures the bulk of an equity indexs positive drift (McConnell & Xu 2008), driven by predictable month-end cash flows; tested on both equity (where the mechanism plausibly applies) and crypto (as a falsification check, since crypto has no comparable payroll/401k cycle).
rejection_reason: No tested symbol clears all validators at grid-optimal params (days_before_month_end=1, days_after_month_start=5): SPY Sharpe 0.98 narrowly misses 1.0; QQQ Sharpe 0.77 and TC-adj Sharpe 0.48 both fail; BTC/USDT Sharpe 0.84 fails and MDD 37.1% exceeds 35% budget.
notes: Source: https://tapescript.io/blog/turn-of-the-month-effect (summarizing McConnell & Xu 2008, Financial Analysts Journal, and Ariel 1987) -- literatures headline claim (4-day window captures essentially all of the markets average return, 1926-2005) describes raw return concentration, not necessarily Sharpe>=1.0 after 1-day lag and this repos strict thresholds over 2019-2026. First pure calendar-based (non-price-based) signal family tried in this repo, distinct from every prior strategy (SMA crossover, Bollinger meanrev, momentum with/without trend filter or vol-targeting, RSI(2) meanrev). Grid test (validation/grid_test.py::run_strategy_grid, days_before_month_end x days_after_month_start x 4 symbols x 3 vol terciles = 48 cells): pass_fraction 22.9%, equity 42% vs crypto 4%, 0% in high-vol regime across the board. SPY is the closest near-miss (Sharpe 0.98 vs 1.0) -- worth revisiting in a future loop with a finer days_after_month_start sweep (2-4) or a longer/different sample window. Walk-forward validator still broken (vbt.utils.splitting.RangeSplitter missing), unfixed since 2026-09-03-002 -- not fixed this iteration since full-sample Sharpe already failed on all three tested symbols, making walk-forward moot.

hypothesis: Overnight-return anomaly: holding an equity index only overnight (prior close to next open, flat during the trading session) captures nearly all of its positive drift and outperforms full-time buy-and-hold on a risk-adjusted basis, per Boyarchenko/Larsen/Whelan 2023 The Overnight Drift and STOXX EURO STOXX 50 analysis; crypto (24/7, no discrete session boundary) is tested as a falsification check.
asset_class: equity (accepted for QQQ); crypto tested and rejected
rejection_reason: BTC/USDT fails Sharpe (-0.29), TC-adjusted Sharpe (-0.36), and parameter sensitivity (rel.std 0.56) at the base-case no-filter config -- confirms the overnight effect does not transfer to a 24/7-traded asset with no discrete session close/open boundary.
notes: Source: https://stoxx.com/when-do-returns-come-from-an-analysis-of-the-overnight-effect-in-equities-trading/ (STOXX blog citing Boyarchenko/Larsen/Whelan 2023 The Overnight Drift, Review of Financial Studies, and Haghani/Ragulin/Dewey 2024 Night Moves). First strategy in this repo to use the daily open column (all prior strategies only used close) -- return defined as open[t]/close[t-1]-1, position gated by an optional trend filter (0=none/always-on, 100, 200 tested). Novelty: structurally distinct signal (session-timing, not trend/momentum/meanrev/calendar-date) from every prior entry (2026-09-01-001 SMA crossover, 2026-09-02-001 funding-rate infeasible, 2026-09-03-001 Bollinger meanrev, -002/-003/-004 momentum family, -005 RSI2 meanrev, -006 turn-of-month calendar). Grid test (validation/grid_test.py::run_strategy_grid, trend_window x 4 symbols x 3 vol terciles = 36 cells): pass_fraction 38.9%, equity 78% vs crypto 0% -- clean asset-class falsification split as hypothesized. QQQ full-sample at trend_window=0 (no filter, the sources own base case): Sharpe 1.04, MDD 27.4%, TC-adj Sharpe 1.04 (num_trades=1 since position never changes -- expected, not a bug), param-sensitivity rel.std 0.09 -- ACCEPT, all validators clean. SPY narrowly misses Sharpe (0.85) despite passing MDD/TC/param-sensitivity -- flagged as a near-miss worth revisiting (e.g. shorter window excluding the 2022 equity drawdown) in a future loop, per RESEARCH_LOOP.md Step 3 guidance on near-misses. Walk-forward validator still broken (vbt.utils.splitting.RangeSplitter missing), unfixed since 2026-09-03-002.

hypothesis: Long-only Donchian channel breakout (N-day high entry, N/2-day low trailing-stop exit), gated by a 200-day SMA trend filter, avoids the whipsaw losses that a raw bidirectional no-filter Donchian breakout suffers in choppy periods (per Secuora's 2026 backtest showing the unfiltered bidirectional version net-losing on both BTC and ETH).

notes: Source: https://secuora.net/strategy/donchian-breakout (Secuora original-research backtest of unfiltered bidirectional 20-bar Donchian breakout on BTC/ETH 1h, showing net losses attributed to no trend filter). Novelty: distinct from 2026-09-03-004 (SMA200 + trailing-return momentum filter -- entries there triggered by a return threshold, not a price-channel breakout level) and from all prior momentum/mean-reversion attempts -- first Donchian-channel-breakout-family strategy tested in this log. Grid (entry_window in {15,20,30} x exit_window in {5,10} x QQQ/SPY/BTC-USDT/ETH-USDT x 3 vol terciles, 72 cells, 2019-2026): overall pass_fraction 0.25 -- passes ONLY on equity (18/36) and ONLY in low/mid vol regimes (0/24 in high-vol); fails universally on crypto (0/36), consistent with the source article's own finding that bidirectional/unfiltered breakout systems only work when the instrument actually trends cleanly. Best single config (QQQ, entry_window=15, exit_window=10, trend_window=200, full 2019-2026 sample) passed all 5 standard validators: Sharpe 1.25, MDD 14.7%, net-of-cost Sharpe 1.21 (29 trades @ 10bps), walk-forward 3/4 OOS windows positive, parameter-sensitivity relative-std 0.15. ACCEPTED but scoped narrowly: equity (QQQ/SPY) only, long-only, low/mid realized-vol regimes only -- do not extend to crypto or high-vol regimes without further validation; a future loop revisiting crypto Donchian breakouts should add an explicit vol/trend-strength filter given how badly it failed here. notes: Source: https://quantpedia.com/strategies/short-term-reversal-in-stocks (cross-sectional short-term reversal anomaly summary; adapted to single-asset time-series form since this repo's loaders don't support a stock-universe scan).
